slides.text: Welcome to lectures twenty seven and twenty eight: dimensionality reduction. P C A, L D A, t-S N E and U M A P, and V I F.

Lecture twenty seven is about fewer, cleaner features: multicollinearity and V I F, the idea of P C A, variance explained, and interpreting components. Lecture twenty eight is about labels and pictures: L D A, the classification view, t-S N E and U M A P for pictures only, and which method when. Our data is Wine Quality: six thousand four hundred ninety seven wines, red and white, with eleven lab measurements.

Multicollinearity is when one feature can be predicted from the others. The density of wine depends on its sugar and its alcohol, so density adds almost no new information. In regression, linked features make the weights unstable and hard to read. A correlation heat map only checks pairs; V I F checks each feature against all the others. V I F equals one over one minus R squared, where R squared says how well the other features predict this one.

On the wine data, density has a V I F of fifteen point nine, residual sugar seven point two, fixed acidity four point nine, and alcohol four point eight. The guide: one means no link, one to five is moderate and usually fine, five to ten is high, check it, and above ten is serious. Drop density and the largest V I F falls to two point eight. Or use P C A, whose components always have V I F equal to one.

Principal Component Analysis rotates the data to new axes. P C one is the direction in which the data spreads the most. P C two is the next biggest spread, at ninety degrees to P C one. Keep a few, since the first few P Cs hold most of the information. Each P C is a weighted mix of all features, P Cs are uncorrelated, and P C A does not use the target.

Always scale before P C A. P C A chases the biggest variance. Unscaled, total sulfur dioxide, with a standard deviation of fifty seven, beats density, with a standard deviation of point oh oh three. P C one explains ninety five percent just because of units. After standard scaling, every column has standard deviation one, and P C one explains twenty seven point five percent.

How many P Cs? The scree plot shows bars of percent explained and a line of cumulative percent. Three rules: the elbow of the scree plot suggests three; the Kaiser rule, eigenvalue above one, gives three; and reaching ninety percent of variance needs seven. P C one plus P C two hold fifty percent of the information in eleven features.

To interpret components, read the loadings. A loading is the weight of a feature in a P C, and you read the largest positive and negative weights. P C one has sulfur dioxide and sugar on one side and volatile acidity and chlorides on the other: white style versus red style. P C two has density against alcohol: heavy versus light. P C three has citric and fixed acidity against pH: acidity.

Check the name: P C A never saw the wine type. Yet red wines sit on the left, with an average P C one of minus two point five, and white wines on the right, with plus point eight. P C one really is a red versus white style axis.

Reading a biplot has three rules. Arrows in the same direction mean the features rise together, like the two sulfur dioxides. Opposite directions mean one rises while the other falls, like density and alcohol. And points lie towards the features they are high in.
Lecture twenty eight: using labels to separate classes, and drawing pictures of clusters.

L D A reduces dimensions to separate classes. P C A does not use class labels and finds directions of largest spread; L D A uses labels and finds directions of best class separation. L D A's maximum components is the number of classes minus one. P C A is used to compress and explain; L D A to classify. For example, quality grouped as low, medium and high is three classes, so L D A gives two components.

L D A beats P C A at classification. Using the same two dimensions to predict quality group, two L D A components give fifty seven point seven percent test accuracy, two P C A components give forty eight point six, and always guessing medium gives forty three point six. L D A chose its dimensions to separate the classes.

t-S N E and U M A P are for pictures only. They keep neighbours close, giving clear clusters, as in two thousand red and white wines. But the axes have no meaning, gaps and sizes are not reliable, the picture changes with the random seed and settings, and t-S N E cannot place new rows.

Which method when? To find and fix linked features: V I F, then drop, or use P C A. To compress features and keep the meaning: P C A with loadings. To separate known classes or classify: L D A. To look at clusters in a picture: t-S N E or U M A P. To feed a model: P C A or L D A, never t-S N E.

Key takeaways. V I F above ten is serious multicollinearity; density scored fifteen point nine. For P C A, scale first; P C one plus P C two hold fifty percent of eleven features. Name each P C from its largest loadings. And L D A uses labels, while t-S N E and U M A P are for pictures only. Thanks for watching.
